title: Senior/Staff/Principal Engineer
description: Canonical is a leading provider of open source software and operating systems to the global enterprise and technology markets. Our platform, Ubuntu, is very widely used in breakthrough enterprise initiatives such as public cloud, data science, AI, engineering innovation, and IoT. Our customers include the world's leading public cloud and silicon providers, and industry leaders in many sectors. The company is a pioneer of global distributed collaboration, with 1200+ colleagues in 75+ countries and very few office-based roles. Teams meet two to four times yearly in person, in interesting locations around the world, to align on strategy and execution. The company is founder-led, profitable, and growing. This is a general track for Senior+ (Senior/Staff/Principal) Engineers in any team at Canonical. After the first round of interviews we will establish which teams might be an excellent fit, and progress your application with them. At Canonical a Senior+ Engineer is not only an outstanding software architect and coder, they also demonstrate the leadership qualities needed to rally a team or department to ship outstanding products. A Senior+ Engineer partners with other Engineering leaders (Managers, Directors, VPs) to take joint responsibility for outcomes at team, department and company level. We hire based on academic results and proven execution, and we select those with a passion for open-source software, innovation, and cutting-edge technology. In this role, you will make a significant contribution in Canonical's portfolio through high-quality code, technical leadership, team motivation and direction, exceptional design, and crisp documentation. As a Senior+ Engineer you'll drive the architecture, design and evolution of high-impact open source software. Our teams work at every level of the stack. From the kernel and system software at the core of Ubuntu through to major language runtimes and the bleeding-edge of cloud automation and distributed systems, you'll have the opportunity to work on complex but highly rewarding projects. Our teams also build the services which deliver Ubuntu to the world, on cloud, devices, servers and PCs. Additionally, this role will give you the opportunity to engage with the broader open-source community. We're looking for individuals who can help build a thriving community, contribute to a broad range of technologies, and ensure seamless software operations at scale. Location: we have remote opportunities for Senior Engineers in every time zone. The role entails Leading design and architecture of an impactful open source project Coding in Golang, Rust, Python, C/C++ or Typescript / React Collaborating proactively with a globally distributed team Mentoring, developing and advising colleagues in their career progression Displaying technical leadership in Canonical and our communities Debugging issues and producing high-quality code to fix them Contributing to technical documentation with the aim to make it the best of its kind Working from home with global travel twice annually for company events What we are looking for in you An exceptional academic track record from both high school and university Undergraduate degree in Computer Science or STEM, or a compelling narrative about your alternative path Drive and a track record of going above-and-beyond expectations Technical leadership as well as team motivation, direction and pace Deep experience with at least one of Go, Rust, Python or C Conscientiousness and detail orientation, with a focus on performance Excellent communication skills including professional written and spoken English Excellent interpersonal skills, curiosity, flexibility, and accountability Ability to travel twice a year, for company events up to two weeks each Nice-to-have skills Depending on your eventual team, you might also bring experience with Container technologies such as LXD, Docker and Kubernetes Highly concurrent, distributed systems Performance engineering – from kernel to web – benchmarks, optimization Software security – fuzzing, tabletop threat models, analysis, audit Build systems and toolchains, including for cross-compilation Public clouds or OpenStack Debian/Ubuntu packaging Systems programming or scalable web services Deep quality and test engineering Web or Flutter front-end experience REST and gRPC API experience SQL and NoSQL data store expertise What we offer you We consider geographical location, experience, and performance in shaping compensation worldwide. We revisit compensation annually (and more often for graduates and associates) to ensure we recognize outstanding performance. In addition to base pay, we offer a performance-driven annual bonus or commission. We provide all team members with additional benefits which reflect our values and ideals. We balance our programs to meet local needs and ensure fairness globally. Distributed work environment with twice-yearly team sprints in person Personal learning and development budget

title: Community Engineer (multiple roles and seniority levels)
description: Our ambition is to set a standard of excellence when it comes to serving the open source ecosystem. This is your chance to be a part of that as a Community Engineer at Canonical . We are building community management at scale. We have multiple positions available, at different seniority levels. All applications and candidates are handled through this single entry point. To improve your chances of success in this application, read our advice on how to get a job at Canonical. The role of a Community Engineer The Community team at Canonical enables community leaders and participants to get things done, co-ordinating with Canonical teams and ensuring that community processes are efficient and well run. We don't do the work of the community, but we facilitate that work to ensure that energetic and ambitious community members with their own vision of open source can benefit from the work Canonical does and bring their own flavor of Ubuntu into being, to meet the needs and express the interests of their community. You will play a key role in designing, executing, and scaling initiatives that foster a thriving community. This is an exciting opportunity for a technically proficient person who is passionate about open source software, Linux, and sustainable community building. In this role, you will support community initiatives with your technical skills and strong organizational skills. You work hand in hand with developers to smooth processes and integrate community plans with Canonical plans for maximum impact. You can encourage and facilitate the creation of new technical projects that enhance the community contribution experience, and you represent community interests to Canonical teams. You will lead complex, multi-disciplinary programs from conception through launch, working closely with Developer Relations engineers, technical authors, product managers, marketing teams, engineering teams, and external partners. You will support and engage with volunteer developers in the Ubuntu community, addressing their concerns and helping them to create successful tools. You will help to ensure their success and the overall autonomy and sustainability of projects. You will provide the content and technical support to ensure the community stays engaged and informed. This will include regular blog and social media posts about community initiatives, events, accomplishments, and collaborative efforts between Canonical and the Ubuntu community. You will communicate effectively with developers and software engineers and represent not only the Ubuntu community but Canonical as a contributor to the wider Linux ecosystem. Our team attends conferences and expos, and talks about technical community projects and their development processes. Location : These are fully remote roles, open to candidates across the globe. title: General Manager – Ethiopia
description: Role Overview CIMC Tianda is seeking a locally based General Manager to lead its airport equipment installation and maintenance operations in Ethiopia. The successful candidate will take overall responsibility for the local team and airport service contracts, covering business performance, customer relations, installation management, operations and maintenance, HSE, personnel and subcontractor management. The position requires a hands-on manager who can maintain reliable airport operations while supporting the continued development of the local business. Key Responsibilities Assume overall responsibility for local business performance, including budgeting, profit and loss, cost control, cash flow and operating forecasts. Manage airport maintenance contracts, ensuring compliance with contractual requirements, SLAs and equipment availability targets. Manage airport equipment installation projects, including installation planning, site coordination, manpower arrangements, subcontractor management, progress control, quality, safety, testing, commissioning and handover. Oversee preventive and corrective maintenance, 24/7 breakdown response, spare parts, maintenance records and subcontractor performance. Maintain effective relationships with the airport, customers, government authorities and other local stakeholders. Support business development, contract renewals, quotations, variations, claims, invoicing and accounts receivable collection. Lead the local organization, including recruitment, shift arrangements, training, performance management and employee relations. Implement HSE and safety management systems, ensuring compliance with airport requirements and local regulations. Monitor contract profitability and implement measures to improve installation efficiency, operational performance and service quality. Submit regular business, financial and operational reports in English to the Regional Director. Coordinate major commercial, technical, installation and personnel matters with the Regional Director and headquarters. Mandatory Requirements Must have held a middle-management or above position at Addis Ababa Bole International Airport. This must have been an actual employment role based at the airport, with responsibility for airport operations, ground handling, airport equipment or GSE maintenance, or on-site contracted services. Project supply, installation work or occasional contact with the airport as a customer does not meet this requirement. Proven experience managing operational teams, technicians, shifts and subcontractors. Working knowledge of airport operations, installation and maintenance management, service-level requirements and safety management. Demonstrated ability to manage budgets, operating costs and customer relationships. Able to lead business discussions and prepare management reports in English. Based in Addis Ababa or able to work there permanently, with the legal right to work in Ethiopia. Willing to remain available for major operational issues outside normal working hours. Preferred Qualifications Previous General Manager, Operations Director, Country Manager or equivalent experience. Experience with passenger boarding bridges, GSE or other electromechanical airport equipment. Experience in full P&L management, installation project management, contract negotiation, claims and collections. Familiarity with Ethiopian employment practices and airport stakeholder management. Application Please submit an English CV clearly stating the employer, job title, employment dates and responsibilities for the middle-management or above role held at Addis Ababa Bole International Airport. Please also indicate your notice period, earliest available start date and salary expectations.

title: Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL) and Research Manager - Integrated Innovation Highway (IIH) Project Ethiopia
description: PATH current employees - please log in and apply Here PATH is a global nonprofit dedicated to achieving health equity. With more than 40 years of experience forging multisector partnerships and with expertise in science, economics, technology, advocacy, and dozens of other specialties, PATH develops and scales up innovative solutions to the world’s most pressing health challenges. PATH combines scientific and public health expertise, implementation experience, innovation, and strong partnerships with governments, communities, civil society, and development partners. In Ethiopia, PATH works closely with the Federal Ministry of Health (MoH), Regional Health Bureaus, health facilities, communities, local organizations, and development partners to strengthen health systems and expand access to high-quality, equitable health services. Project Overview The Integrated Innovation Highway (IIH) is a Gates Foundation–funded project that supports the Government of Ethiopia (GoE) and MoH to establish a government-owned platform that systematically identifies country needs, prioritizes innovations, assesses evidence and readiness, and supports the introduction, transition, and scale-up of innovations within the Ethiopian health system. The IIH will establish an integrated approach across six innovation highways: Medical devices Diagnostics Therapeutics, family planning and nutrition products Vaccines Technology, including digital health, artificial intelligence (AI), and biotechnology Bundled and systems innovations Phase 1 will focus on three tracer products across two highways: Medical devices: AI-enabled point-of-care ultrasound (AI-POCUS) Diagnostics: Near-point-of-care TB PlusLife and Ebola diagnostics The project will work closely with the MoH, Regional Health Bureaus, public health institutes, universities, innovators, development partners, and other stakeholders to strengthen innovation governance and develop practical pathways for evaluating, introducing, transitioning, and scaling priority health innovations. Position Summary The Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, and Learning (MEAL) and Research Manager will provide strategic and technical leadership for the project's monitoring, evaluation, research, learning, and adaptive management functions. The MEAL and Research Manager will lead the design, implementation, and continuous improvement of the project's MEAL system, ensuring that project performance, evidence, learning, and lessons are systematically generated, analyzed, communicated, and used to inform decision-making and the transition and scale-up of health innovations. The position will work closely with the Project Director, IIH technical team, MoH, Regional Health Bureaus, research institutions, universities, local partners, innovators, and other stakeholders to generate and use evidence to inform the introduction, transition, and scale-up of priority innovations. Reporting and Working Relationships Reports to: Project Director, Integrated Innovation Highway Key internal relationships: IIH Project Director, technical leads, Project Officers, AI/innovation specialists, PATH Ethiopia leadership, finance and operations teams, and PATH global/regional technical teams. Key Responsibilities MEAL System Design, Data Management, and Performance Monitoring Lead the design, implementation, and maintenance of the IIH MEAL system, aligned with the work plan, learning agendas, results framework and donor requirements. Develop and maintain project indicators, performance measurement plans, data collection tools, reporting templates, and data management systems. Establish systems for tracking project outputs, outcomes, milestones, risks, assumptions, and progress toward transition and scale-up goals. Oversee implementation monitoring at national, subnational, partner, and service-delivery levels, as applicable. Ensure timely collection, analysis, validation, and reporting of project performance data. Support the development and monitoring of annual and quarterly project work plans. Learning, Evaluation, and Adaptive Management Analyze project data and lead performance reviews and learning sessions to assess progress against targets, identify implementation bottlenecks, emerging risks, and lessons learned, and recommend corrective actions to support adaptation and continuous improvement. Lead the development and implementation of learning agendas and priority learning questions for the IIH. Lead evaluations of the project and its approaches, and support stakeholders to interpret and use evaluation findings. Work with technical leads and project partners to ensure that evidence, learning, and evaluation findings are routinely used to inform project implementation and strategic decisions. Research and Evidence Generation Lead the development of the project's research and evidence-generation agenda and coordinate its implementation with project and research partners. title: Business Development Coordinator
description: The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future. The IRC has a focus on narrowing the gender gap in humanitarian aid and ensuring that we contribute to gender equality, diversity, and inclusion in both our programs and operations by working to establish a context where our clients (including those from minority groups) enjoy the same rights and opportunities as well as an equal access to services. The IRC also has a strong commitment to creating an equitable and inclusive culture, where safeguarding is upheld in our workplace and programs. We are determined to protect our clients and staff from safeguarding violations through prevention and, where misconduct is alleged, to address it without fear or favor. Job Overview/Summary Based in Addis Ababa, the Business Development Coordinator owns the design and development of assigned funding proposals for the IRC Ethiopia program, from opportunity assessment through to contract signature. The role reports directly to the Deputy Director for Grants and Partnerships (DDGP) and works in close partnership with the Senior Business Development Coordinator, who owns business development strategy, the opportunity pipeline and donor relationships. The Coordinator acts as proposal lead on assigned opportunities. This means convening and facilitating the technical design process, writing concept notes and proposal narratives, managing the proposal team and consortium partners day to day, and assuring the quality, compliance and on-time submission of the full package. The Coordinator is accountable to the DDGP for the quality and timeliness of every submission they lead, works with minimal direction, and escalates early when decisions, resources or deadlines are at risk. The successful candidate will have a strong track record of leading proposal development with multilateral and bilateral donors in humanitarian and international development contexts, combining technical design skill and exceptional writing with the ability to coordinate many contributors under tight deadlines. Major Responsibilities Include Pipeline and opportunity intelligence Research and maintain current donor briefs on funding priorities, strategies, funding windows and geographic interests relevant to IRC Ethiopia, and give them to the Senior Coordinator and the DDGP to inform donor strategy and positioning. Identify, qualify and track new opportunities across technical sectors and donors, including the private sector and philanthropy, and keep the opportunity pipeline and the Go/No-Go (GNG) tracker accurate at all times. Prepare opportunity assessments for GNG meetings covering donor fit, competitiveness, partners, resources and risk, and present them with the Senior Coordinator, who owns the GNG process. Record decisions in the tracker and make sure every relevant team is informed. Draft pre-emptive funding pitches and concept notes for priority opportunities as directed by the Senior Coordinator, working with technical teams. Technical design on assigned proposals Lead Project Design Meetings for assigned proposals, from half-day sessions to multi-day workshops, applying the design standards set by the Senior Coordinator. Prepare the agenda, pre-reads and facilitation plan, brief participants on donor expectations and compliance requirements, facilitate evidence-based prioritization of activities, and close each meeting with documented decisions, owners and next steps. Own the intervention logic of each assigned proposal. With the MEAL team and technical leads, develop the theory of change and results framework or logframe, with explicit risks, assumptions and mitigation measures. Test technical designs for feasibility, evidence base, donor compliance, cost-effectiveness and internal coherence, including bringing multi-objective or multi-sector designs together into one logic. Resolve disagreements between technical, regional and donor priorities, and escalate to the DDGP those that cannot be resolved. Ensure designs reflect IRC’s commitments on gender equality, inclusion, protection and safeguarding, conflict sensitivity and accountability to affected people, as well as any cross-cutting requirements set by the donor.
